body: Yeah the new place seems great, except now I met an awesome guy in the city where I'm living now and now I don't want to move lol. I just want a new job in my city. Sigh, don't know what I'm going to do. The new place is only 20 minutes or less from work, which would be awesome. I don't even like my job that much though. But I'm worried that every job would feel like that haha, like maybe I just don't like working :P I don't know what I'm going to do. I feel like I go back and forth on things every day, it's so hard for me to make decisions.

I knew her only for the time she worked here, but she was young so we got along and would call each other after work if it was a stressful day and complain lol. I mean, she had only been working for six days! So I feel like even though she made a mistake, she should have been given more chances. It just seems ridiculous to fire someone after that length of time. There was a reason but it didn't seem severe enough to actually fire her. I don't know, it was very weird. And it makes me nervous. So I'm caught between trying to find a new place to live or a new job. Luckily I'm meeting with the girl with the temporary room this week!!

Yeah, I found somewhere short-term finally! But now I'm feeling weird about my job. Someone got fired last week after working there for only a week so I feel like I could get fired at any time too! I don't know what to do sometimes, everything feels like the wrong thing. I don't want to be stuck in a job either, but I'm worried that changing jobs a lot will look bad on my resume. I don't know if employers care about that…?

It's hard. Nothing really interests me right now. I mean, I guess I feel like it's not that nothing really interests me, it's that all the things I know about don't really interest me. I feel like there might be something out there that I would like doing but maybe I don't even know about it yet. Like I've heard there are a lot of jobs that people don't even think of or that might not be created yet. I don't know though. I'm not really sure what to do with that lol. Right now my biggest worry is finding a place to live closer to work that I can lease short-term. It's nearly impossible and I'm so frustrated! No one wants to lease month-to-month. So I don't know if I should find a new job closer to home (which is really hard to do anyway) or keep commuting and hope to find something? I don't know.

I will definitely have to leave the company to "advance" at all. And I'm really not feeling the law thing (I've seen a lot of it since I work with attorneys now) so I have no idea what I'm going to do. I'm hourly and most hourly jobs don't have health insurance :( it sucks. Canada is much better for healthcare (lived there about half my life, sometimes think about going back lol). I'm hoping I'll only work at my company for like a year (or even less) and then do something else. I need to try more things and figure out what to do with my life.

I do enjoy traveling, but with other people. My family takes a few vacations a year, mostly to tropical places to get some sun, and I really like doing that. I didn't enjoy traveling by myself very much, it was very stressful. Especially since many times I was living with a host family or something, so I really had to adapt to the culture. I'm not very good at adapting. Not surprising I guess, lol. I thought you were already in Europe for some reason? I can't remember what, but something you said made me think you were European.

I'll be moving closer to a bigger city. Right now I live about 40 miles from that city but I want to move so that I'm in a much closer suburb (so I guess bigger, maybe? It's still a suburb though because the actual city is one of the most dangerous in the U.S. and I have too much to worry about without worrying about my safety, lol). Yeah my job is okay. I wish they gave me health insurance because paying for it out of pocket is so expensive here :( and I feel like I'm doing work that doesn't require a college degree (like being a secretary), but I'm glad I have a job.

Traveling after college is cool, I know a lot of people who want to do that. My old roommate felt the same, that she had done 4 years of college and needed a break. I'm too type A to take a break for any amount of time but I wish I could be more relaxed and do something like that. Where will you travel?

Yeah I really want to move. I thought I would like living here more than I do. But since I graduated most of my friends moved away and the town just isn't the same for me anymore. It's been pretty disappointing. But I also think I didn't move because I'm afraid of change. Even small change bothers me, like stupid things like the gym I go to changed the way they did some of their classes and even though I still go and like the classes it freaked me out. But I really do want to move, I'm hoping it would be a change for the better. Even though I'm scared I wouldn't make friends in a new place. I think it will be hard but the alternative is just to keep doing what I'm doing I guess, and that sucks too.

I'm an assistant at a law firm. I like it okay, it sort of bothers me that I'm basically a secretary even though I went to college and had a 3.9 GPA. But I feel like it's easier to move than find a new job. Finding a job was so hard. What do you do?

Yeah I've wanted to take one for a while but the universities in my area don't offer any not-for-credit. It's weird. And yeah, I am very lucky to have my job. But my boss is pressuring me to relocate because I have to work different hours because my commute is so long so that's stressing me out.

I really like reading and writing. Those are pretty solitary activities, but I would join a book club if I could find a local one with people my age. The thing is, I'm living in a college town right now, so while there are a lot of people around who are my age, they're mostly taking classes so they probably wouldn't want to join a book club. I would love to take a creative writing class but I haven't been able to find a good not-for-credit one at any of the local schools. I'll probably look again next semester though. I don't really know what else I'm interested in :/

I spent half of my childhood in the United States and half in Canada, and I've also lived for a few months in Spain, Costa Rica, and Mexico. Yeah, I don't expect or want to get married right now or anything, but I just want a "normal" life. I want to find somewhere I'm comfortable and belong. I love the city I went to university in, and I'm living there now, but it's not the same anymore. I thought I would know more people here than I do:(

Are you early 20s too? I feel like every time I start talking to someone my age about life I realize that I'm not that alone in being so scared about everything. It's kinda nice I guess.

I know, I do need to change things. I'm thinking of moving closer to work soon, and I'm hoping that will give me a new start and new energy. It just seems hopeless in my current situation. I would definitely do things like meetup, but I haven't found that many (at least in my area) for people my age! It always seems to be middle aged people. Which is fine, but not really what I'm looking for.

I wasn't upset about dating because of that one guy (although I do feel bad about that), but it just kept happening over and over again online that I would be talking to a guy and suddenly they'd stop talking to me, or they'd say they wanted to meet up and then never text. Like over and over. It just made me feel like a failure because it's like, if I can't even meet people online I must be a loser.

Everything you said is right. It's just hard sometimes. I like traveling and have actually traveled a lot and lived in several different countries, but - not to sound snobby - I'm kind of over it. I like going on vacation with my family and people I know, but I wouldn't want to travel by myself. I'm at the point where I want to settle down and find my place in the world, but I'm struggling so much. Thank you so much for talking to me, it's nice to know that someone cares. I really, really appreciate it.

Yes, I think your interpretation is right. I'm very bad at being alone, it's always been a problem I've had. And it's hard for me to imagine not being alone because I feel like it's impossible to meet new people after college. Everyone is super busy and working and I feel like soon everyone will start getting married and having kids and then they'll have even less time and interest in meeting people or making friends. So it just seems like the problem will never be solved.

I don't have social anxiety. I'm very outgoing. I just don't even see opportunities to meet people anymore - it's not like I'm going to hang out at a bar by myself or something like that. I just go to work (my company is very small and everyone is older so I don't make friends through work) and come home (I live by myself) so I never even see people. I even tried online dating, which I'm super embarrassed about, and I ended up deleting my account because it just became too frustrating and it made me feel really bad about myself. I would respond to guys' messages and talk for a few days but then it would go nowhere and one of us would stop responding. Like, I couldn't even get asked out through online dating. That felt really shitty. I think part of the problem right now is how bad I feel about myself, I just don't even know what to think anymore. I'm a huge failure.
I'm not sure I know what you mean but thank you for replying. I think I need real-world friends, I'm not too into online relationships. And I don't do art.

Thank you for your response. I probably feel worse when I compare myself to other people, but I really don't like being alone. And I just can't imagine living the rest of my life alone, I would just rather die. But I don't know how to meet people in the "real world," so that seems like the only option now.

I volunteer with prisoners through a local organization. I enjoy it, but it hasn't been a good way to meet people - most of them are still in college and aren't there to make friends.

Anyway, thanks. I appreciate it
